clue.text: To provide the final insult get a learner driver's plate

definitions.meaning: to top everything off with one last offence
the plate on a British learner's car shows a big red letter L

explanation.surface: Someone, already insulted, is told to stick an L-plate on their car as the last straw.
explanation.walkthrough: Second sense read cryptically: the L on a British learner driver's plate is a capital letter, CAPITAL L, which sounds out the phrase when run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means crowning a series of misfortunes; the plate carries one upper-case letter.

clue.text: A lot of crowing must be going on despite the fiasco

definitions.text: A lot of crowing must be going on despite the fiasco

parts.words: A lot of crowing must be going on despite the fiasco
parts.note: crowing birds raised up suggests roosters standing tall, while the phrase is slang for a muddle

explanation.surface: Someone boasts loudly though things have gone badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Roosters with heads up crowing are the literal picture; the British slang phrase means a botched job.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a blunder or mess, built from the image of roosters raised up.

clue.text: Summary of the former USSR?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or earlier
the Commonwealth of Independent States, CIS, followed the USSR, so the USSR is the state before the CIS

explanation.surface: A digest of Soviet history.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the old Soviet Union came before the CIS, so it was 'pre-CIS'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short abstract of a text is an outline or digest.

clue.text: Rich cake included in breakfast or tea

indicators.note: the cake is contained within the words that follow, sitting across them

explanation.surface: Indulgent gateau served at breakfast or teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich layered continental gateau, often with nuts or chocolate.

clue.text: I get ill, all upset, over boy having an affaire

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits above the next one
in a down clue both pieces turned upside down are read from the bottom up

parts.note: to ail is to be ill
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone sick with worry because their son is having an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all upset' turns I plus AIL upwards to give LIAI, which goes over SON. 'affaire' is the French spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit romantic relationship, an amour.

clue.text: Become reconciled to war paint

definitions.meaning: to settle a quarrel and be friends again
jocular term for cosmetics

explanation.surface: Two foes settle their differences over warpaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means patch up a quarrel; the noun is cosmetics, jokingly called war paint.

clue.text: Everyone peering over precipice is nervous

parts.note: all means everyone
standing at a cliff's brink is being at the very rim

explanation.surface: A group looking over a cliff all feel jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means tense and jittery.

clue.text: When trained on it pears lie in an orderly fashion

definitions.text: When trained on it pears lie in an orderly fashion

indicators.note: the letters are set out neatly in a new order

explanation.surface: Pear trees grown flat against a frame lie neatly in rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in an orderly fashion' rearranges PEARS LIE, and the whole clue describes the trellis used for training fruit trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice on which fruit trees are trained flat, as pears are.

clue.text: Expecting a reigning prince

parts.note: regnant means ruling, as in a queen regnant

explanation.surface: A ruling prince is expecting a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' here means with child, not awaiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying a baby, a synonym of expecting.

clue.text: Obvious method to find a road where parking is prohibited

definitions.text: a road where parking is prohibited

parts.note: something obvious is clear
a method is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A driver looks for an easy way to find a no-parking road.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLEARWAY is a British road on which vehicles may not stop or park.
explanation.definitionFit: A British road classification banning stopping, so parking is forbidden along it.

clue.text: How the hours pass when composedly asleep

indicators.note: read as 'com-posed', put together anew, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hours slip by calmly while someone sleeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composedly' looks like calmly, but read as re-composed it asks for ASLEEP to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse as it goes by; the phrase describes that passing of hours.

clue.text: Forte piano run

parts.note: f is the musical abbreviation for forte, loud
piano in music means soft, quiet or low

explanation.surface: A musical instruction: loud, soft, then a fast run.
explanation.definitionFit: To stream or pour is to run, as liquid does.

clue.text: If it goes in a car, the car won't go everywhere

definitions.text: If it goes in a car, the car won't go everywhere

parts.words: If it goes in a car, the car won't go everywhere
parts.note: the word also means applying everywhere

explanation.surface: A riddle about a car part whose absence leaves the car going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The universal joint carries drive in a car; without it the car will not move, and the word itself means everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means applying in all places, and is also the name of a car's drive joint.

clue.text: Yarn in which New York fellow leaves London

indicators.note: the fellow departs from the city's name, so those letters are taken out of it

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A tale of a New Yorker who quits London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' suggests a story, but it is the textile sense. 'leaves' removes DON from LONDON, leaving LON.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic fibre spun into thread, so a kind of spun thread.

clue.text: Maybe Spike Milligan is to take the stage

definitions.meaning: Spike Milligan was one of the ... of the BBC radio comedy The ... Show
to make one's entrance as a performer

explanation.surface: Will the comedian Spike Milligan come on stage?
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a 1950s British radio comedy; its performers, Spike Milligan among them, were the Goons.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of that comedy troupe is a goon; a performer entering the stage goes on.

clue.text: Shilling gambler just a bit up on the others

definitions.text: just a bit up on the others

parts.note: in old British money a shilling was said as 'one', as in a price of one and six
a gambler is someone who bets

explanation.surface: A small-stakes punter edging ahead of rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin; prices were read out as 'one and six' for one shilling and sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means slightly surpassing others, outdoing them.

clue.text: A variety of winged duck caught inside

definitions.text: A variety of winged duck caught inside

indicators.note: one piece is held within another, like something trapped indoors
a variety is a different arrangement, so the letters of the next word are shuffled

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A breed of duck has been caught indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A variety of' rearranges WINGED to WIDGEN, and 'caught inside' puts O (a cricket duck, zero) within it; the whole clue also describes the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild duck species, so the clue's winged duck fits it.

clue.text: Primate swallowed vegetables and died with hunger satisfied

indicators.note: the next piece follows on at the end
the primate eats the vegetables, so they go inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
peas are vegetables
d is the abbreviation for died in records

explanation.surface: An ape ate vegetables and died, though no longer hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunger quelled means sated or placated.

clue.text: Disturbed by rumour being spread

definitions.meaning: upset or troubled
a story circulated as gossip is spread around

explanation.surface: Someone upset by gossip going round.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means upset or inconvenienced, and also circulated as gossip.

clue.text: The destitute, upper class appearing in the press

indicators.note: the class shows up within the newspapers, so its letter sits inside them

parts.note: newspapers collectively are the papers
U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: The poor and the posh both feature in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'upper class' comes from the 1950s U and non-U distinction in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor people with nothing are the needy, a synonym.

clue.text: Secure place to keep valuables

definitions.meaning: protected from harm
a strongbox for money and jewels

explanation.surface: A secure spot for keeping precious things.
explanation.definitionFit: Protected from danger; also a locked strongbox.

clue.text: Lead spoons may in Yuri Geller's hands

definitions.meaning: an electric cable or cord

definitions.text: spoons may in Yuri Geller's hands
definitions.meaning: Uri Geller claimed to bend spoons by mind power

explanation.surface: A trick involving spoons bending for a famous psychic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' wants to be the metal; it is an electric cord. Geller was famous for spoon-bending shows.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric cord is a flex in Britain; to bend is also to flex.

clue.text: Argue the danger of dirty nuclear bombs

definitions.meaning: to quarrel

definitions.text: the danger of dirty nuclear bombs
definitions.meaning: radioactive debris spread by a blast

explanation.surface: Debating the hazards of radioactive weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarrel with someone; also the radioactive dust a nuclear blast scatters.

clue.text: Rules governing diocesan clerks

definitions.meaning: church laws or principles
clergy attached to a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: Regulations that govern cathedral clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Church laws are rulings; cathedral clergy are also given the same title.

clue.text: Said 'No 'resolutely to a handsome chap

indicators.note: read as 're-solute-ly', dissolved and remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone firmly refused a good-looking man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolutely' looks like firmly, but it signals rearranging SAID NO. In Greek myth the youth loved by Aphrodite was famously beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the mythical youth, the word means a very good-looking man.

clue.text: Transport from the East but not in time

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East
something not on time is late

explanation.surface: Goods carried in from the East arrive behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like carriage, but here it is the verb to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to fill them with joy, a synonym.

clue.text: Pension for all the directors

definitions.meaning: a boarding house or room-and-meals arrangement in a European guest house
the complete board of a company

explanation.surface: A pension arrangement for an entire company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pension' looks like retirement pay, but it is the French boarding-house sense, where meals are included.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodging with all meals is the European pension arrangement; a whole board means every director present.

clue.text: Shattered as a result of being bankrupt

definitions.meaning: smashed to pieces
having no money

explanation.surface: Someone devastated after going bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed is the past participle sense; out of money is the slang sense.

clue.text: Drinks and makes piggish noises

definitions.meaning: a snort is a quick shot of spirits
pigs grunt by forcing air through their noses

explanation.surface: Someone who drinks heavily and grunts like a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Shots of spirits are tots; pigs make loud nasal grunts.

clue.text: Make a great effort to leave the country

definitions.meaning: to do something lavishly or thoroughly
to travel from the countryside into the city

explanation.surface: Trying very hard to emigrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave the country' suggests emigrating, but it means quitting rural life for the town.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means spend lavishly or put in effort; literally, heading into the urban centre.

clue.text: Plant information around an archaeological site

indicators.note: the information surrounds the site, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: data is facts or information
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city excavated in Iraq

explanation.surface: Collecting plant records near a dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of poisonous flowering shrubs such as thorn apple.

clue.text: Highlights single hair

parts.note: tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Getting highlights in a single hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlights' suggests hairdressing, but it is the verb meaning emphasises.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise points is to underline them, a synonym of the verb.
